Package installation and activation


File downloading

```{r}
#download the file
download.file(
  url = "https://mothur.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/wiki/miseqsopdata.zip",
  destfile = here::here("data/miseqsopdata.zip"))

#unzip the to get individual fastq files
unzip("data/miseqsopdata.zip", exdir = 'data/')
#record path to data
data_dir <- here::here("data/MiSeq_SOP")
list.files(data_dir)

read.delim(base::paste(data_dir,"mouse.dpw.metadata", sep = "/" ))[
  order(read.delim(base::paste(data_dir,"mouse.dpw.metadata", sep = "/" ))[[2]]),]
```

Question 1

Perform a quick QC check by examining all forward and reverse file charts

Take all files, sorted into forward (Fs) and reverse (Rs)

```{r}
fnFs <- sort(list.files(data_dir, pattern="_R1_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))
fnRs <- sort(list.files(data_dir, pattern="_R2_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))
#basename removes the folder names
sample.names <- stringr::str_split_fixed(basename(fnFs),"_",2)[,1]

```

Plot all forwards. Best to examine in seperate tab.

```{r}
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[1:length(fnFs)])
```

Plot all reverses. Best to examine in seperate tab.

```{r}
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[1:length(fnFs)])
```

Filtering Reads: Sanity Check

```{r}
#Filter trims using DADA2
#First create destination folders for final output
#R1
filtFs <- here::here("outputs/filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_F_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtFs) <- sample.names
#R2
filtRs <- here::here("outputs/filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_R_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtRs) <- sample.names

#Use filterAndTrim to filter reads. truncLen specifies for (forward, reverse) lengths
#maxN must be set to 0 for DADA2 processing later
#maxEE is maximum number of expected errors, which has better filtering than raw quality score
#truncQ means reads are truncated whenever the Q score is elow the int
#m.phix means any reads marked as from the phiX genome are discarded
#compress means final files are gzipped
#multithread allows multiple files to be processed at once. With an int, it uses that many cores. Disabled on Windows
out <- filterAndTrim(fnFs, filtFs, fnRs, filtRs, truncLen=c(240,160),
                     maxN=0, maxEE=c(2,2), truncQ = 2 ,rm.phix=TRUE,
                     compress=TRUE, multithread = TRUE)
out2 <- as.data.frame(out) %>% mutate(prop = (100*(reads.out/reads.in)))
head(out2)
results <- ""
results <- paste(results, "Mean percent of sequences left:", mean(out2$prop))
results <- paste(results, "Minimum percent of sequences left:", min(out2$prop))
results <- paste(results, "Lowest number of reads:", min(out2$reads.out))
#results
```

```{r}
errR <- learnErrors(filtRs, multithread=T)
```

Pair Merging

```{r}
#Use DADA2 to find true sequences from false duplicates during PCR
dadaFs <- dada(filtFs, err=errF, multithread = TRUE)
dadaRs <- dada(filtRs, err=errF, multithread = TRUE)

#Merge paired ends together
mergers <- mergePairs(dadaFs, filtFs, dadaRs, filtRs, verbose=TRUE)
#Inspect the merger data.frame from the first sample
#DT::datatable(mergers$F3D0,options = list(scrollX = TRUE, autoWidth = TRUE))

#Tabulate previous data
seqtab <- makeSequenceTable(mergers)
#dim(seqtab)

#Note: since the region identified is 250 - 260bp long, should check for suspicious-length ASVs
#table(nchar(getSequences(seqtab)))
```

Chimera Removing

```{r}
#Remove chimeras
seqtab.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab, method="consensus", multithread=F, verbose=TRUE)
#Proportion ASVs were removed due to chimeras?
chimera_removal_results <- ""
chimera_removal_results <- paste(chimera_removal_results, "Percent of variants chimeric:", 100-(dim(seqtab.nochim)[2]/dim(seqtab)[2]*100))
chimera_removal_results <- paste(chimera_removal_results, "Percent of merged sequence reads chimeric:", 100 - sum(seqtab.nochim)/sum(seqtab)*100)
#chimera_removal_results
```

Filtering Final Result Check

```{r}
#Simply checking how much data was filtered
#Ideally, each sample still have 1000+ reads, and keep most of their reads
#getN simply sums how many unique things there are, in this case sequences
getN <- function(x){ 
  sum(getUniques(x))
}

#track holds all variables that are tracked, 
track <- cbind(out, sapply(dadaFs, getN), sapply(dadaRs, getN), sapply(mergers, getN), rowSums(seqtab.nochim))
colnames(track) <- c("input", "filtered", "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nonchim")
rownames(track) <- sample.names

track <- as.data.frame(track) %>% mutate(prop_kept = round(nonchim/input*100,2))
DT::datatable(track)
```

Table Formatting

```{r}
#Simply make table easier to look at and use
#Turn matrix into dataframe, replacing column names with ASV sequence numbers
ASV_tbl <- as.data.frame(seqtab.nochim) %>% 
  `colnames<-`(base::paste("ASV", seq(1:ncol(seqtab.nochim)), sep = ""))
DT::datatable(ASV_tbl, options = list(scrollX = TRUE, autoWidth = TRUE))

#Remove the mock data used for sanity
ASV_tbl <- as.data.frame(t(ASV_tbl[-nrow(ASV_tbl),]))
ASV_tbl <- ASV_tbl %>% mutate(rs = rowSums(ASV_tbl)) %>% 
  filter(rs > 0) %>% dplyr::select(-rs)
```

```{r}
#Using DNAStringSet from Biostrings to read the seqs 
ASV_seqs <- DNAStringSet(base::colnames(seqtab.nochim) %>% 
                           `names<-`(base::paste("ASV",seq(1:ncol(seqtab.nochim)),sep = "")))
```

Taxonomic Assignment

```{r}
#Assign taxonomy to sequences
#SILVA dataset used, as it is the best-maintained and curated rRNA data set
#By default, cutoff for bootstrapping confidence is 50%, thus NULL is used for any place that is <50% confident
taxa <- assignTaxonomy(seqtab.nochim, here::here("data/silva_nr99_v138.1_wSpecies_train_set.fa.gz"), multithread=TRUE)

#Convert taxa matrix into dataframe for ease of reading
taxa2 <- as.data.frame(taxa) %>% 
  `row.names<-`(base::paste("ASV", seq(1:nrow(taxa)), sep = ""))

#Remove non-prokaryotic ASVs
taxa2 <- taxa2 %>% filter(Family != "Mitochondria") %>% filter(Order != "Chloroplast")
taxa3 <- taxa2 %>% mutate(ASVs = row.names(taxa2)) %>% dplyr::select(ASVs, everything())

#Format ASV table to allow joining to taxonomic table
ASV_tbl2 <- ASV_tbl %>% mutate(ASVs=row.names(ASV_tbl)) %>% dplyr::select(ASVs, everything())

#Join taxanomic table to ASV table
taxa3 <- taxa3 %>% inner_join(ASV_tbl2, by = "ASVs")

#Use taxa2 for futrue Phyloseq and filter ASV_tbl for later
taxa2 <- taxa2 %>% filter(rownames(taxa2)%in%taxa3$ASVs)
ASV_tbl <- ASV_tbl %>% filter(row.names(ASV_tbl) %in% taxa3$ASVs)

#See how much of each taxonomic division is present as a percent
taxa3[,(ncol(taxa2)+2):ncol(taxa3)] <- sweep(
  taxa3[,(ncol(taxa2)+2):ncol(taxa3)],2,
  colSums(taxa3[,(ncol(taxa2)+2):ncol(taxa3)]),'/')*100

#Simply check if all divisions adds to 100
#colSums(taxa3[,(ncol(taxa2)+2):ncol(taxa3)])

#Clean ASV table and export to FASTA
ASV_seqs[names(ASV_seqs)%in%ASV_tbl2$ASVs]
if(!file.exists(here::here("outputs/mouse_ASVs.fa"))){
  writeXStringSet(ASV_seqs[names(ASV_seqs)%in%ASV_tbl2$ASVs], here::here("outputs/mouse_ASVs.fa"))
  readLines(here::here("outputs/mouse_ASVs.fa"))[1:10]
}
```

Sanity Check: Mock Data

```{r}
#Checking how well DADA2 handles the mock data
#How many sequences were in the mock? 20 expected
unqs.mock <- seqtab.nochim["Mock",]
unqs.mock <- sort(unqs.mock[unqs.mock>0], decreasing=TRUE) # Drop ASVs absent in the Mock
cat("DADA2 inferred", length(unqs.mock), "sample sequences present in the Mock community.\n")

#How many of the unique sequences from above match their expected? Hopefully a perfect 20/20
mock.ref <- getSequences(file.path(data_dir, "HMP_MOCK.v35.fasta"))
match.ref <- sum(sapply(names(unqs.mock), function(x) any(grepl(x, mock.ref))))
cat("Of those,", sum(match.ref), "were exact matches to the expected reference sequences.\n")
```

Phyloseq Analysis

```{r}
#Read data from file
mdta <- read.delim(base::paste(data_dir,"mouse.dpw.metadata", sep = "/" ))

#Compare data from file with data processed
#Are the sample names similar to the sample names we have in the ASV table?
#length(mdta$group %in% colnames(ASV_tbl))
#Set row names and massage table 
mdta <- mdta %>% mutate(category = if_else(dpw > 100 , "Late","Early")) %>% 
  mutate(gender = if_else(str_detect(group, "F"),"F","M")) %>%
  mutate(subject = str_extract(str_split_fixed(group, "D", 2)[,1],"(\\d)+")) %>%
  `row.names<-`(mdta$group)

#Generating the phyloseq object
#phyloseq requires ASV/OTU table, a taxa table, a Biostrings StringSet, and a metaData table
ps <- phyloseq(otu_table(as.matrix(ASV_tbl), taxa_are_rows=T), 
               sample_data(mdta), 
               tax_table(as.matrix(taxa2)))
ps <- merge_phyloseq(ps, ASV_seqs)

#Lets calculate richness and diversity
#Shannon and Simpson are diversity estimators, ACE is a richness estimator, observed is how many ASVs we have (198)
rnd <- estimate_richness(
  ps, measures=c("Observed", "ACE","Shannon", "Simpson")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-se.ACE)
```

Question 4

```{r}
write.csv(rnd, "Diversity_of_Species_Richness.csv")
```

Visualizing Diversity

```{r}
#Plot data
rnd <- rnd %>% mutate(group = row.names(rnd))%>% inner_join(mdta, "group")
#make a long table
rndl <- rnd %>% gather("Estimator", "Value", 1:4) %>% 
  mutate(rd = if_else(Estimator == "Observed" | Estimator == "ACE", 
                      "Richness","Diversity"))
```

Question 5

```{r}
#Use RColorBrewer to make the final chart color-blind safe
library(RColorBrewer)
palette <- brewer.pal(n = 4, "Set2")
ggplot(rndl, aes(x=dpw, y=Value, color = Estimator, fill= Estimator))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge())+
  facet_grid(rd~category, scales = "free")+
  theme_bw()+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette)
ggsave("Diversity_and_Richness.pdf", plot = get_last_plot(), height = 12, width = 12)
```

Plotting Seperation of Early and Late Samples

```{r}
# Log transforming the data prior to using bray curtis so that overly abundant ASVs will not skew the results
ps.prop <- transform_sample_counts(ps, function(otu) log1p(otu))
#Perform the ordination
ord.nmds.bray <- ordinate(ps.prop, method="NMDS", distance="bray")
plot_ordination(ps.prop, ord.nmds.bray, color="category", title="Bray NMDS")
```

Plotting Changes in Taxa From Start to End

```{r}
top20 <- names(sort(taxa_sums(ps), decreasing=TRUE))[1:20]
ps.top20 <- transform_sample_counts(ps, function(OTU) OTU/sum(OTU)*100)
ps.top20 <- prune_taxa(top20, ps.top20)
plot_bar(ps.top20, x="dpw", fill="Family") + facet_wrap(~category, scales="free_x") +
  ylab("Relative abundance (% of seqs/sample)")
```

Plotting Richness of Individual Families

```{r}
#Make the taxa table relative to each other, representing in percentages
fam <- as.data.frame(taxa3 %>% dplyr::select(Family, where(is.numeric)) %>% 
                       group_by(Family) %>% summarise_all(sum))
#head(fam)
#Sanity check: does it sum to 100%?
#colSums(fam[,2:ncol(fam)])

#Perform the same for all families of low-abundance, aka <1 represented
fam_o <- fam
fam[2:ncol(fam)][fam[2:ncol(fam)]<1] <- 0
fam_o[2:ncol(fam_o)][fam[2:ncol(fam_o)]>1] <- 0
Others <-colSums(fam_o[2:ncol(fam_o)])
fam[nrow(fam)+1,2:ncol(fam)] <- Others
fam[nrow(fam),1] <- "Others"
#tail(fam)

#Get a long table needed for ggplot2
fam_l <- fam %>% gather("group","relab",2:ncol(fam)) %>%
  inner_join(mdta,"group")

txplot <- ggplot(fam_l, aes(x = dpw, y=Family, size = relab))+ 
  geom_point()+
  facet_wrap(~category, scales = "free_x")
txplot
```
